review_scope: Worst-case time complexity labels for the exact frozen Java source snippets below.

assumptions: Each vertex is marked visited before it is enqueued.
Each vertex is enqueued and processed at most once.
Each adjacency entry is examined at most once.
Hash-set operations are expected O(1); queue operations are O(1).
E counts adjacency entries under the graph representation convention.
cases.rationale: Each vertex is processed at most once and each adjacency entry is examined at most once.

conditional_simplification.assumption: S <= V, where S is the number of entries in starts.

initialization_and_duplicate_start_verif.finding: The starts loop performs one expected O(1) set-add attempt per input entry. HashSet.add returns true only for a previously unseen seed, so duplicate starts are not enqueued. The initial queue therefore contains each distinct start once.
initialization_and_duplicate_start_verif.review_gate: Satisfied by source inspection before recording this artifact.

assumptions: links is an adjacency-list representation backed by a map whose lookup is expected O(1).
Hash-set operations are expected O(1); deque operations are O(1).
Each distinct start is enqueued once because seen.add(seed) guards enqueue.
Each subsequently discovered vertex is enqueued once because seen.add(there) guards enqueue.
Each processed vertex adjacency entry is examined at most once.
S is the number of entries in starts; E counts graph adjacency entries.
cases.rationale: Initialization costs O(S), the traversal processes at most V vertices and scans at most E adjacency entries, yielding O(S + V + E). If S <= V, this simplifies to O(V + E). Duplicate entries in starts do not cause repeated enqueueing or repeated adjacency scans.
